basics.label: Comprehension
basics.value: [f(x) for x in rows if keep(x)]

patterns.title: Index once, look up many
patterns.why: Replace repeated scans with one dictionary index.
patterns.remember: A dictionary is the standard repeated key-lookup pattern.

patterns.title: Stream with a generator
patterns.why: Process streams incrementally instead of materializing everything.
patterns.remember: Use yield for files, API pages and large record streams.

apis.name: enumerate
apis.example: for i, row in enumerate(rows, start=1): ...

apis.name: zip
apis.example: for name, score in zip(names, scores): ...

practices.title: Deduplicate in order
practices.prompt: Keep the first occurrence of each event_id.
practices.reveal: Maintain a set for membership and append only unseen IDs.

patterns.title: Readable method chain
patterns.code:
result = (
    orders
    .query("status == 'paid'")
    .assign(revenue=lambda d: d["qty"] * d["price"])
    .groupby("country", as_index=False)
    .agg(revenue=("revenue", "sum"))
)
patterns.why: Keep a transformation visible top to bottom.
patterns.remember: Method chains work best when each step changes the same DataFrame conceptually.

patterns.title: Validate joins
patterns.code:
enriched = orders.merge(
    customers,
    on="customer_id",
    how="left",
    validate="m:1",
    indicator=True,
)
patterns.why: Join cardinality bugs can silently multiply rows.
patterns.remember: validate and indicator make assumptions explicit.

patterns.title: Latest row per business key
patterns.code:
latest = (
    events
    .sort_values(["customer_id", "updated_at"])
    .drop_duplicates("customer_id", keep="last")
)
patterns.why: Sort explicitly, then keep one deterministic winner per key.
patterns.remember: In Pandas, latest-row logic is usually sort_values + drop_duplicates.

apis.name: assign
apis.whatFor: Add derived columns in a chain.

practices.title: Latest order per customer
practices.prompt: Keep one newest order per customer.
practices.reveal: Sort by timestamp descending, then drop_duplicates on customer_id.

patterns.title: Expression pipeline
patterns.code:
result = (
    df
    .filter(pl.col("status") == "paid")
    .with_columns((pl.col("qty") * pl.col("price")).alias("revenue"))
    .group_by("country")
    .agg(pl.col("revenue").sum())
)
patterns.why: Expressions give Polars room to optimize and parallelize.
patterns.remember: Think column expressions, not row-wise Python.

patterns.title: Lazy scan
patterns.code:
result = (
    pl.scan_parquet("events/*.parquet")
    .filter(pl.col("event_date") >= cutoff)
    .select(["user_id", "amount"])
    .group_by("user_id")
    .agg(pl.col("amount").sum())
    .collect()
)
patterns.why: Lazy scans can push filters and projections down.
patterns.remember: Use scan_* for analytical file pipelines and collect at the boundary.

patterns.title: Latest row per business key
patterns.code:
latest = (
    df
    .sort(["customer_id", "updated_at"])
    .unique(subset=["customer_id"], keep="last")
)
patterns.why: Ordered unique selection expresses a compact top-one-per-key pattern.
patterns.remember: Sort by the tie-breaker first, then unique on the business key.

practices.title: Latest row per user
practices.prompt: Read large Parquet and keep latest event.
practices.reveal: Scan lazily, filter early, sort by event time, then keep one row per user.

technologies.name: Spark / PySpark
technologies.tagline: Partitions, shuffles, joins and DataFrame execution.

basics.label: Rule
basics.value: Watch shuffle, skew and tiny files

patterns.title: Latest row per key
patterns.code:
w = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(F.col("updated_at").desc())

latest = (
    df
    .withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(w))
    .filter(F.col("_rn") == 1)
    .drop("_rn")
)
patterns.why: Window functions express ordered per-key logic without collecting.
patterns.remember: row_number is the standard deterministic dedupe shape.

patterns.title: Broadcast small dimension
patterns.code:
result = fact.join(
    F.broadcast(dim),
    on="country_id",
    how="left"
)
patterns.why: Broadcast can avoid shuffling a large fact relation.
patterns.remember: Broadcast only genuinely small data and confirm the plan.

practices.title: Skewed aggregation
practices.prompt: One key owns 40% of rows.
practices.reveal: Confirm skew first, then consider salting or a different aggregation plan.

technologies.name: PySpark
technologies.tagline: Spark DataFrame patterns expressed through Python APIs.

basics.label: Rule
basics.value: Prefer Spark built-ins over Python UDFs

patterns.title: Latest row per business key
patterns.code:
w = Window.partitionBy("customer_id").orderBy(
    F.col("updated_at").desc()
)

latest = (
    df
    .withColumn("_rn", F.row_number().over(w))
    .filter(F.col("_rn") == 1)
    .drop("_rn")
)
patterns.why: Window functions express ordered per-key logic without collecting data to the driver.
patterns.remember: Use row_number for deterministic deduplication when you have a clear ordering column.

patterns.title: Prefer built-in Spark expressions
patterns.code:
clean = df.withColumn(
    "email_domain",
    F.lower(F.element_at(F.split(F.col("email"), "@"), -1))
)
patterns.why: Built-in expressions stay inside Spark's optimized execution engine.
patterns.remember: Check pyspark.sql.functions before reaching for a Python UDF.

practices.title: Incremental CDC dedupe
practices.prompt: Keep only the newest record per primary key.
practices.reveal: Partition by the business key, order by sequence/timestamp descending, then keep row_number = 1.

technologies.tagline: DAG design, retries, schedules and task boundaries.

patterns.title: TaskFlow DAG
patterns.why: TaskFlow keeps dependency wiring close to Python.
patterns.remember: Tasks should be meaningful retryable operational boundaries.

practices.title: Backfillable daily ingestion
practices.prompt: Rerun one day safely.
practices.reveal: Parameterize writes by the logical interval and make them idempotent.

technologies.tagline: SQL models, ref/source, incremental logic and tests.

patterns.title: Thin staging model
patterns.code:
select
  cast(order_id as bigint) as order_id,
  cast(order_ts as timestamp) as order_ts,
  amount
from {{ source('raw', 'orders') }}
patterns.why: Normalize names and types close to the source.
patterns.remember: Keep staging mechanical; move business meaning downstream.

patterns.title: Incremental lookback
patterns.why: Process changes while tolerating late arrivals.
patterns.remember: Incremental logic must remain correct on a full refresh.

practices.title: Late-arriving facts
practices.prompt: Source can revise 48 hours.
practices.reveal: Use a safety window and merge on a stable unique key.

basics.label: CTE
basics.value: with base as (...) select ... from base

basics.label: Conditional agg
basics.value: sum(case when ... then amount else 0 end)

patterns.title: Latest row per key
patterns.why: Ranking windows solve deterministic top-N per group.
patterns.remember: Partition defines the group; order defines the winner.

patterns.title: Anti-join
patterns.code:
select s.*
from source_rows s
left join target_rows t
  on t.id = s.id
where t.id is null;
patterns.why: Find rows present on one side and absent on the other.
patterns.remember: NOT EXISTS is an equally useful anti-join shape.

apis.name: ROW_NUMBER
apis.example: row_number() over (partition by id order by ts desc)

apis.name: LAG
apis.example: lag(status) over (partition by id order by ts)

practices.title: Consecutive activity
practices.prompt: Find gaps between user events.
practices.reveal: Use LAG(event_ts) partitioned by user and compare timestamps.

patterns.title: Query files directly
patterns.why: Query columnar files without loading them into a server database.
patterns.remember: Push filters and projections into the scan.

practices.title: Local lake query
practices.prompt: Aggregate partitioned Parquet without ingestion.
practices.reveal: Query the glob directly and filter before aggregation.

technologies.name: Delta Lake
technologies.tagline: Transactional lakehouse merge and history patterns.

basics.label: MERGE
basics.value: merge into target using source on ...

patterns.title: Idempotent upsert
patterns.code:
merge into silver.customers as t
using updates as s
on t.customer_id = s.customer_id
when matched and s.updated_at > t.updated_at then
  update set *
when not matched then
  insert *;
patterns.why: MERGE applies insert/update logic atomically.
patterns.remember: Stable keys and ordering guards matter for CDC.

practices.title: CDC upsert
practices.prompt: Ignore older late updates.
practices.reveal: Update only when the incoming sequence/timestamp is newer.

patterns.title: Latest row with QUALIFY
patterns.why: QUALIFY filters window results without wrapping the query in another CTE.
patterns.remember: BigQuery latest-row = ROW_NUMBER + QUALIFY.

patterns.title: Latest child row with OUTER APPLY
patterns.code:
select c.customer_id, x.status, x.updated_at
from dbo.customer c
outer apply (
  select top (1) s.status, s.updated_at
  from dbo.customer_status s
  where s.customer_id = c.customer_id
  order by s.updated_at desc
) x;
patterns.why: OUTER APPLY is a useful SQL Server-specific top-one-per-parent shape.
patterns.remember: Use OUTER APPLY when you want the parent preserved even without a child row.
